name: flagellar type III export gate
description: Membrane-embedded export gate that translocates the axial subunits of the flagellum (rod, hook and filament) across the cytoplasmic membrane. Without it no axial structure can be built.

name: flagellar export ATPase complex
description: Cytoplasmic ATPase complex that delivers export substrates to the gate. FliJ is deliberately not required: it is a small, poorly conserved escort whose orthology assignment is unreliable, and requiring it would report absent machinery in genomes that build flagella.

name: flagellar MS ring
description: The membrane and supramembrane ring that nucleates basal body assembly and houses the export apparatus.

name: flagellar basal body rod
description: The drive shaft that transmits torque from the motor across the cell envelope to the hook, together with the rod-MS ring junction protein.

name: flagellar C ring and switch complex
description: The cytoplasmic ring that couples the stator to the rotor and switches rotational sense. FliY, which replaces FliN in some Firmicutes, is not accepted as evidence because its KEGG orthologue K02424 is assigned to an L-cystine transport binding protein and is therefore not specific to the flagellar switch.

name: flagellar hook
description: The curved universal joint that transmits torque from the rod to the filament. FlgD is excluded because it is a transient assembly scaffold rather than a part of the finished structure.

name: flagellar hook-filament junction
description: The hook-associated proteins that adapt the hook to the filament; without them flagellin polymerises without being retained.

name: flagellar filament
description: The helical propeller: polymerised flagellin together with the distal cap that permits its ordered polymerisation.

name: flagellar stator torque generator
description: The membrane-anchored ion-conducting stator units that generate torque against the C ring. The curated claim is deliberately silent about the coupling ion; see the description of SYS_SF_FLAGELLAR_STATOR_MOTAB.

name: flagellar L and P rings
description: The outer membrane and peptidoglycan bushings through which the rod passes in a diderm envelope. Monoderms build a flagellum without them, which is why they belong to a separate architecture rather than being an optional part of one.

name: type IV prepilin peptidase
description: Cleaves and N-methylates the type IV prepilin leader, without which no pilin can be polymerised.

name: type IVa major pilin
description: The subunit polymerised into the pilus fibre.

name: type IVa pilus assembly ATPase
description: The cytoplasmic motor ATPase that powers pilus extension.

name: type IVa pilus inner membrane platform
description: The polytopic inner membrane protein that transfers pilin subunits from the membrane into the growing fibre.

name: type IVa pilus alignment subcomplex
description: The envelope-spanning subcomplex that aligns the inner membrane platform with the outer membrane secretin.

name: type IVa pilus secretin
description: The outer membrane channel through which the pilus fibre emerges.

name: type IVa pilus retraction ATPase
description: The ATPase that depolymerises the fibre. It is accessory to assembling a pilus and is therefore not required by the architecture; a genome without it is expected to build a pilus it cannot retract.
